subject: microbiology
title: Bacitracin Sensitivity, PYR and Group A Streptococcal Identification

steps.tx: The **bacitracin sensitivity test** places a 0.04 unit bacitracin disc on beta haemolytic colonies: any inhibition zone presumptively identifies group A pyogenes (its wall synthesis unusually bacitracin tender), while groups C and G usually resist. Modern benches confirm with PYR or latex grouping because a minority of non A strains share sensitivity.
steps.say: A bacitracin zone on beta haemolytic colonies whispers group A; PYR confirms the whisper.

points: Resistant beta haemolytic: group B, C, G thinking

right.title: Confirmation pair
points: Bacitracin never sole evidence in invasive isolates

steps.tx: Beta haemolytic colonies on a blood agar plate are tested with a tiny antibiotic disc. The **bacitracin sensitivity test** uses 0.04 units of bacitracin, and any zone of inhibition presumptively marks group A Streptococcus pyogenes, whose wall synthesis is unusually sensitive. Groups C and G usually grow up to the disc. Because a few non A strains also show a zone, PYR or latex grouping is used to confirm.

steps.tx: **M protein typing** (emm sequencing of the hypervariable M protein gene) tracks pyogenes epidemiology: rheumatogenic and nephritogenic emm traditions, invasive clones (M1T1 global), vaccine candidate coverage by type distribution. Bench grouping says A; emm says which A is circulating through schools and wards.
steps.say: Group names the tribe, emm names the travelling clan within it.

left.title: emm epidemiology
points: M1 and M12 invasive and pharyngitis classics
Type distributions vary by region and income

right.title: Vaccine arithmetic
points: Multivalent M vaccines cover common emm types
Rheumatic heart burden drives urgency in endemic regions

steps.tx: **Streptococcal superantigens** from the pyogenes cupboard (SpeA, SpeC and kin, several prophage borne) crosslink MHC and TCR as the antigens module described, producing scarlet fever in toxin naive and toxic shock in invasive disease. Phage mobility explains why toxin repertoires differ between emm clones of one species.
steps.say: Scarlet fever is a phage toxin meeting a non immune child, not a different streptococcus.

left.title: Scarlet fever portrait
points: Sandpaper rash, flushed cheeks, circumoral pallor
Strawberry tongue, Pastia lines in folds
Antitoxin antibody protects against rash, not infection

steps.tx: **Spreading factors** dissolve the neighbourhood for pyogenes: hyaluronidase digests ground substance, streptokinase activates plasminogen dissolving clots, DNases liquefy pus (improving spread, thinning abscesses historically treated with streptokinase streptodornase), and C5a peptidase trims neutrophil summons at the surface. Examiners often pair this with streptococcal toxic shock, where the same superantigens act systemically rather than on a child's throat and skin.
steps.say: Dissolve matrix, clot and pus while muting neutrophil calls: spreading is engineered.

left.title: Spreading enzymes
points: DNases A to D: pus viscosity and NETs

right.title: Defence trimming
points: NET degradation by DNase escapes traps

steps.tx: **Throat culture technique** decides pharyngitis answers: swab tonsils and posterior pharynx avoiding tongue, plate on sheep blood agar (selective plates in some laboratories), stab for subsurface haemolysis, incubate and read beta colonies at 24 and 48 hours, group latex from suspicious colonies. Poor swabs grow viridans and call it negative.
steps.say: Swab the tonsils, stab the agar, read twice: throat culture is technique before result.

steps.tx: **Rapid antigen limitations** in children justify culture back up traditions: sensitivity 70 to 90 percent against culture (specificity excellent), negative molecular assays may not need backup where validated, and adults' lower rheumatic risk relaxes backup rules in many guidelines. Geography and rheumatic fever incidence set how strict a programme should be.
steps.say: Negative rapid test in a child earns a culture where rheumatic fever still walks.

left.title: RADT profile
points: Carrier detection flaw shared with culture

right.title: Backup logic
points: Children and adolescents: culture negatives (US tradition)
Endemic rheumatic regions lower testing thresholds

steps.tx: **Invasive group A disease** (necrotising fasciitis, myositis, toxic shock, bacteraemia) demands surgery plus antibiotics: urgent debridement, penicillin plus clindamycin (toxin suppression from the staph lessons), IVIG consideration in toxic shock, intensive support, and public health assessment of contacts in defined clusters. Bench identity becomes a surgical clock.
steps.say: Pain out of proportion plus group A means theatre first; antibiotics escort surgery.

left.title: Necrotising portrait
points: Severe pain, oedema beyond erythema, bullae late
Hypotension and organ failure in toxic shock
Varicella and NSAID debates as risk contexts
Imaging must not delay exploration when suspicion high

right.title: Response stack
points: IVIG in streptococcal toxic shock considered
Household contact advice by jurisdiction protocols

steps.tx: **Invasive group A disease** includes necrotising fasciitis, myositis, streptococcal toxic shock, and bacteraemia. Necrotising fasciitis is a surgical emergency. Pain out of proportion to the skin changes is the clinical alarm, and debridement is urgent rather than optional. Penicillin is paired with clindamycin because clindamycin suppresses toxin production even when the organism is already at high density. Intravenous immunoglobulin is considered in toxic shock. Intensive care supports failing organs. Public health assesses close contacts when a cluster is defined.
steps.say: Necrotising fasciitis, myositis, toxic shock, and bacteraemia are invasive group A streptococcal disease. Pain beyond the visible skin change means theatre, not observation. Penicillin is combined with clindamycin to suppress toxin. Immunoglobulin is considered in toxic shock, with intensive care support. Defined clusters need a public health look at contacts.

vis.alt: A clinical photograph of a leg shows rapidly spreading discoloration of necrotising fasciitis beyond the area that looks merely cellulitic.
vis.caption: Dusky, spreading change on a leg marks deep fascial infection that has already outrun the skin findings and needs immediate surgery. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Bacitracin as drug** footnote completes the disc biography (novobiocin lesson pattern): topical bacitracin ointments survive, systemic use died of nephrotoxicity in the 1940s, its target (bactoprenol recycling in wall synthesis) explains pyogenes tenderness. Many bench discs are wall drugs bacteria met first in patients.
steps.say: Bacitracin blocks wall lipid recycling; too nephrotoxic to swallow, perfect to test with.

right.title: Disc family reunion
points: Each disc is a former or niche drug
